idea.title: Plant Doctor AI
idea.text: My revolutionary app: point your camera at any houseplant and an AI tells you what's wrong and how to fix it. Everyone has plants, everyone will download this!

intake.restatement: A camera app that diagnoses houseplant problems and suggests remedies.
implicit_assumptions: visual symptoms are sufficient to diagnose most plant problems
existing plant-ID apps leave a diagnosis gap worth switching for
users will pay or return often enough to sustain the app
intake.open_question: What does this diagnose that PictureThis and Planta already don't?

judge.verdict: Fine-tuning a vision model on plant-disease datasets is a known path and public datasets exist. The hard part is not the model, it is being usefully better than the incumbents' diagnosis mode.
watchouts: incumbent apps already ship diagnosis features
proposed_tests: benchmark PictureThis on 20 sick plants and count its misses
judge.viable_scope: Diagnosis for the 10 most common houseplants and their 15 most common ailments, nothing else.

believer.verdict: As stated this is a generic template — 'an AI app that helps plant owners'. What's missing is a wedge: a care-reminder loop, a local-nursery tie-in, or a species niche the big apps ignore. Planta shows the category monetizes.
proposed_tests: pick one underserved niche (e.g. orchids) and check incumbent quality there

precedents.name: Planta
precedents.why_comparable: subscription plant-care app with strong retention in the same audience

scientist_eval.verdict: The idea makes no scientific claim — it is a consumer product question, not a research one. No penalty: absence of literature is not a flaw. My opinion is informational only.

skeptic.verdict: PictureThis existing is a data point, not a verdict — the real problem is that the pitch contains no reason to switch. Visual-only diagnosis also has a ceiling: root rot looks like overwatering looks like underwatering.
watchouts: visual symptoms are ambiguous across common ailments
'everyone has plants' is not a retention argument
proposed_tests: ask 10 plant owners what their current app failed to diagnose
test 5 ambiguous symptom photos against a botanist's diagnosis
check 30-day retention benchmarks for plant apps

investor.verdict: The category is real but consolidated; nothing changed recently that reopens it. Timing is the weak leg — this would have been a 2019 bet.
strengths: willingness to pay proven by incumbents
proposed_tests: find one distribution channel the incumbents don't own

strategist.verdict: The angle 'all plants, all problems, everyone' is the default nobody questioned. A weekend team can copy the generic version because the generic version already exists — twice.
strengths: clear first build step if narrowed
watchouts: broad-consumer angle is the crowded one
proposed_tests: validate one narrow audience with real pull
strategist.alternative_angle: Go B2B: a diagnosis API for plant nurseries and garden centers to offer under their own brand — they have the customer trust and no AI team.

judge.verdict: Maintained: the build is real either way; the strategist's B2B angle actually simplifies my dependency picture (one integration partner instead of app-store acquisition).
judge.viable_scope: Top-10 houseplants, top-15 ailments, or the nursery API pilot.

believer.verdict: Maintained at 6 — the B2B nursery angle is the version I believe in: Planta proved consumers pay, but nurseries paying for white-label diagnosis is the uncrowded upside.
believer.revision: maintained, but transferred my conviction to the B2B angle

scientist_eval.verdict: Maintained: still no scientific claim to verify; neutral and informational.

skeptic.verdict: Raised to 5: the B2B angle answers my switching-trigger objection (the nursery brings the users). The diagnosis-ambiguity ceiling remains and applies to both angles.
watchouts: visual diagnosis ambiguity is unsolved in both angles
skeptic.revision: raised 4 to 5: strategist's angle removes the adoption blocker

investor.verdict: Raised to 6 on the B2B version only: nurseries have margin pressure and no tech, that is a real 'why now-ish'. Consumer version stays a 5.
investor.revision: raised 5 to 6 for the B2B angle

strategist.verdict: Maintained on the idea as submitted: my score rates the pitched angle, and the pitched angle is the crowded default. The alternative is where the committee converged.
strategist.alternative_angle: White-label diagnosis API for nurseries and garden centers.

synthesis.consensus: Buildable but undifferentiated as pitched; the committee independently converged on the same fix — narrow the audience or go B2B via nurseries. The scientist is neutral: no scientific claim involved.

disagreements.topic: is the consumer version worth building at all
disagreements.positions: believer: a niched consumer version can still win; strategist: the consumer angle is structurally the crowded default
disagreements.why_it_matters: it decides which version gets built first

synthesis.action: Interview three plant nurseries this week about paying for white-label AI diagnosis before writing any code.
